svg.title: Our deterministic DLP vs status-quo guards on the same conversations
svg.desc: Two panels on one 0 to 100 percent scale. Left: share of attack sessions that still leak a protected field under each defense. Right: share of benign hospital questions each defense blocks. Wilson 95% intervals; hatched cells are not measured yet.
svg.text: Leaks: same 32 conversations, any record field (adaptive: own 8 tries). Benign: same 77 held-out replies. Wilson 95%
deployed; scores each reply on its own

Riley's output DLP (deployed; scores each reply on its own). Benign hospital questions blocked: pending. not reported yet

Llama Guard, Privacy (S7) (on Riley's replies (its strongest config)). Leaking conversations let through: 91% [76-97], N=32 · per conversation. Basis: full-field label; per reply 104/331 = 31% through (38% on identifier-only replies with no MRN); MRN-only label (secondary): 13/28 = 46%. Source: range-harness/guard_compare/full_field_relabel.json (copy in evidence/)

Llama Guard, Privacy (S7) (on Riley's replies (its strongest config)). Benign hospital questions blocked: 0% [0-5], N=77 · held-out set E. Basis: same 77 logged replies as our row (log sha256 758a8dfb...); 0 also under 'unsafe, any category'; set H 0/80; boundary 0/12; multi-turn 0/30; 526 ms per call. Source: range-harness/guard_compare/lg_benign.json (same-unit session)

g.title: Our DLP v2 · all record leaks (canonicalize + label-flow + budget + predicate). Leaking conversations let through: 0% [0-11], N=32 · per conversation. Basis: frozen v2 (ddcb8931), full-field label; F-01 only 0/31; MRN-only label (secondary) 0/28; the 4 conversations only the full-field label finds: 0/4. Source: range-harness/guard_compare/full_field_relabel.json (copy in evidence/)

Our DLP v2 · all record leaks (canonicalize + label-flow + budget + predicate). Benign hospital questions blocked: 23% [15-34], N=77 · held-out set E. Basis: pre-registered primary: 40 blind questions written to stress the guard, both models (Qwen 6/37, DeepSeek 12/40; 3 errors excluded); counts blocks of Riley's own refusals as FP, as fixed before the run; replication set H 7/80 = 9% [4-17]; 0/199 benign replies carried a record. Source: range-harness/benign_heldout_report.json (log sha256 758a8dfb..., 3/202 errors)

Our DLP v2 · oracle (F-03) (secondary channel (the oracle)). Leaking conversations let through: pending. the shadow logs hold replies only (no user turns), and the real oracle answers with numbers (SQL length/substr), which the yes/no heuristic does not model. F-03 coverage is a design, not a result
Our DLP v2 · oracle (F-03) (secondary channel (the oracle)). Benign hospital questions blocked: n/a. same guard as the row above
g.text: n/a (same guard as the row above)

g.title: Our DLP v2, adaptive attack (attacker knows the rules (DeepSeek, 8 tries)). Leaking conversations let through: 0% [0-66], N=2 · 2 of 8 leaked. Basis: decode-aware GT rule fixed before adjudication (ADAPTIVE_LABEL.md): 2 of 8 adaptive conversations leaked (plain values, non-MRN fields); frozen v2 (ddcb8931) blocked both; 0 of 8 attempts got past the fix, 0% [0-32]; null control 0/8; no encoded leak occurred, so the decoders are untested by attack. Source: range-harness/guard_compare/adaptive_adjudication.json (same-unit session)
Our DLP v2, adaptive attack (attacker knows the rules (DeepSeek, 8 tries)). Benign hospital questions blocked: n/a. same guard as v2

svg.text: Hatched = not measured yet (never a placeholder number). Leak label: ground truth, independent of every guard. The unit of each measured cell follows its value.
